title: Hypercontractivity and entropy decay for infinite-dimensional quantum Gibbs samplers
authors: Simon Becker, Cambyse Rouzé, Robert Salzmann
abstract: We derive rates of exponential relative-entropy decay for a broad class of infinite-dimensional quantum Gibbs samplers. A key technical ingredient is a perturbative stability theory for hypercontractive estimates and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities. For suitably chosen dissipative couplings, we obtain exponential entropy decay for full multimode Bose-Hubbard samplers with arbitrary hopping and repulsive density interactions. For harmonically confined quantum Coulomb gases and molecular systems, we prove exponential entropy decay for every fixed finite-rank low-energy truncation of the interaction. Finally, we exhibit a periodic charging model with a positive spectral gap but no finite-time $L^2$-to-$L^p$ bound for any $p>2$.
summary: This work develops theoretical tools to quantify how fast quantum Gibbs samplers approach thermal equilibrium by analyzing the decay of relative entropy. It successfully proves exponential decay rates for several important physical models, such as Bose-Hubbard and Coulomb systems. Crucially, it also establishes a boundary case, showing that a positive spectral gap alone is insufficient to guarantee the strong convergence properties (hypercontractivity) needed for the fastest decay rates.
main_problem: The paper derives rates of exponential relative-entropy decay for a broad class of infinite-dimensional quantum Gibbs samplers used for thermal state preparation.
main_result: Exponential entropy decay rates are established for Bose-Hubbard samplers and harmonically confined quantum Coulomb gases, while also providing a counterexample showing positive spectral gap does not guarantee finite-time hypercontractivity.
method: The analysis heavily relies on quantum Markov semigroups, utilizing hypercontractivity estimates and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities to bound the relative entropy decay.
model_or_system: The study covers general infinite-dimensional quantum Gibbs samplers, including full multimode Bose-Hubbard samplers, harmonically confined quantum Coulomb gases, and a periodic charging model on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$.
